Processing raw ALS data with raw_to_processed

Source: vignettes/raw-to-processed.Rmd
raw-to-processed.Rmd

raw_to_processed() converts raw ALS point cloud files into quality-controlled, standardised outputs following the German AdV naming convention. It handles a full processing pipeline — CRS validation, reclassification, noise filtering, intensity normalisation, spatial indexing, and metadata generation — with optional parallelisation for large datasets.

Basic usage 

library(managelidar)

raw_to_processed(
  path    = "path/to/raw/",
  out_dir = "path/to/output/"
)

path accepts a single file, a directory, a character vector of file paths, or a VPC file. All LAS, LAZ, and COPC formats are supported.

Parameters

Parameter Default Description
path — Input file(s), directory, or VPC
out_dir tempdir() Root directory for point cloud/overview/metadata outputs
log_dir tempdir() Root directory for logfiles and data summaries (independent of out_dir)
epsg 25832L Fallback EPSG when CRS is missing or invalid
region NULL Two-letter state code (e.g. "ni"); auto-detected if NULL
from_csv NULL CSV with acquisition dates for files without valid GPS time
workers NULL Number of parallel workers; see Parallelisation
verbose TRUE Print progress messages

Output structure

Point cloud outputs are written under out_dir/, while logfiles and data summaries are written under the independent log_dir/ (both default to tempdir(), but can point to different locations):

out_dir/
├── pointcloud/
│   └── 3dm_{zone}_{minx}_{miny}_{tilesize}_{region}_{year}.laz
├── metadata/
│   └── 3dm_{zone}_{minx}_{miny}_{tilesize}_{region}_{year}.vpc
└── overviews/
    └── 3dm_{zone}_{minx}_{miny}_{tilesize}_{region}_{year}.webp

log_dir/
└── logfiles/
    ├── processing_log_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.json
    └── summaries_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS/
        ├── files_in/
        │   └── {original_input_name}.json
        └── files_out/
            └── 3dm_{zone}_{minx}_{miny}_{tilesize}_{region}_{year}.json
Directory Contents
pointcloud/ Processed LAZ files with embedded spatial index (.lax)
metadata/ Per-file VPC files with extended STAC-compatible metadata
overviews/ WEBP images of maximum elevation, coloured with the viridis palette
logfiles/ JSON processing log per run, plus a timestamped summaries_.../ subfolder of per-file summaries

Each run gets its own timestamped summaries_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS/ subfolder. files_in/ uses the original input filename before AdV renaming. files_out/ uses the generated AdV-compliant filename.

Filename convention

Output files follow the AdV standard:

3dm_{zone}_{minx}_{miny}_{tilesize}_{region}_{year}.laz

For example: 3dm_32_547_5724_1_ni_2023.laz

The year is derived from the GPStime of the first point in the point cloud if possible, and from median GPStime or header information otherwise. The region code is either supplied via the region parameter or auto-detected by intersecting tile centroids with federal state boundaries.

If GPS time is unavailable or invalid, a from_csv table of acquisition dates can also be used as a fallback. The source of the date is recorded in the VPC metadata under date_source ("gpstime_median", "gpstime_first_point", "header_creation_year" or "csv").

CRS handling

The function validates the CRS of each file before processing. A CRS is considered invalid if it is missing (0), unrecognised (e.g. 32767), or not resolvable by sf::st_crs(). When an invalid CRS is detected, lasR::set_crs() is prepended to the pipeline using the epsg fallback.

# Files from a campaign stored without CRS — set explicitly (default)
raw_to_processed(
  path = "path/to/raw/",
  out_dir = "path/to/output/",
  epsg = 25832L
)

Classification reclassification

Raw ALS data from German federal states often uses non-standard classification schemes (AdV or legacy LGLN). raw_to_processed() automatically detects the scheme from class proportions and converts to ASPRS standard before further processing:

  • Legacy LGLN — detected when class 13 represents > 1 % of points
  • AdV — detected when class 20 represents > 10 % of points
  • ASPRS / unclassified — no reclassification applied; only undefined classes above 22 are collapsed to unclassified (1)

Parallelisation

Processing runs sequentially for fewer than 20 files and in parallel for 20 or more, using half of available logical CPU cores by default. The number of workers is always capped at half the available cores to leave headroom for memory and system processes.

# Force sequential processing regardless of file count
raw_to_processed(path = "path/to/raw/", out_dir = "path/to/output/", workers = 1L)

# Use a specific number of workers (capped at half available cores)
raw_to_processed(path = "path/to/raw/", out_dir = "path/to/output/", workers = 4L)

# Default: auto (parallel for >= 20 files, sequential otherwise)
raw_to_processed(path = "path/to/raw/", out_dir = "path/to/output/")

Parallel workers are spawned via mirai and load the managelidar package automatically. Each worker processes one file independently; errors in individual files are caught and recorded in the log without affecting other files.

Resuming interrupted runs

raw_to_processed() reads existing log files in log_dir/logfiles/ at startup and skips any input files that were already processed successfully. This means interrupted runs can be resumed simply by calling the function again with the same arguments — only failed or unprocessed files will be re-attempted.

# First run — processes all 50 files; 3 fail
raw_to_processed(path = files, out_dir = "path/to/output/")

# Second run — skips 47 successful files, retries the 3 failed ones
raw_to_processed(path = files, out_dir = "path/to/output/")

Output validation and rollback

If any expected output is missing or empty after processing, all outputs for that file are deleted before the error is recorded. This prevents partial results from accumulating across runs and ensures that a file listed as failed in the log truly has no outputs on disk.

Expected outputs checked per file:

  • .laz in pointcloud/
  • .vpc in metadata/
  • .webp in overviews/
  • .json in logfiles/summaries_.../files_in/
  • .json in logfiles/summaries_.../files_out/

The processing log

Each run writes a timestamped JSON log to logfiles/. The log records the function call, package and dependency versions, all parameters, and a per-file entry with status, duration, and any error messages.

{
  "processing": { "timestamp_start": "...", "duration_seconds": 123.4 },
  "parameters": { "out_dir": "...", "epsg": 25832 },
  "files": [
    {
      "input": "path/to/raw/tile.laz",
      "output": "path/to/output/pointcloud/3dm_32_547_5724_1_ni_2023.laz",
      "status": "success",
      "duration_seconds": 45.2
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "files_total": 20,
    "files_processed": 19,
    "files_failed": 1
  }
}

Possible status values:

Status Meaning
success All outputs written and validated
success_with_warnings Processed successfully, non-fatal warnings raised
skipped_existing Output already present from a previous run
skipped_locked Another parallel worker is currently writing this output
failed Processing failed; all partial outputs removed

Return value

raw_to_processed() returns a list of output file paths (one per input file) invisibly. Failed files return NULL in the corresponding position.

results <- raw_to_processed(
  path    = "path/to/raw/",
  out_dir = "path/to/output/"
)

# filter to successful outputs
successful <- Filter(Negate(is.null), results)
